inputs.prompt: You are preparing the privacy impact assessment (EFVP) draft of a Québec firm, before a project that touches personal information. Firm: {{inputs.firmName}}. Project: {{inputs.projectName}}. Purpose: {{inputs.purpose}}. Personal information involved: {{inputs.personalData}}. People concerned: {{inputs.peopleConcerned}}. Hosting or communication outside Québec: {{inputs.outsideQuebec}}. Safeguards already planned: {{inputs.safeguards}}. Write the sections: 1 Purpose and necessity, 2 Personal information and people concerned, 3 Flows and hosting (say whether a communication outside Québec calls for its own assessment). Write in {{inputs.language}} (fr = Québec French, en = English). The very first line of your answer is exactly this sentence in that language: fr: « Brouillon préparé par Orazaka — ce n'est pas un avis juridique : la personne responsable de la protection des renseignements personnels ou un avocat doit le valider avant tout usage. » en: « Draft prepared by Orazaka — not legal advice: the person in charge of the protection of personal information or a lawyer must validate it before any use. ». Use only the facts given; never invent a fact about the firm, mark anything missing as « À confirmer » (fr) or « To confirm » (en). You prepare, you never decide: the person in charge decides. Cite your sources by reference only, never by quoting a text: the Act respecting the protection of personal information in the private sector (RLRQ, c. P-39.1) as amended by Law 25 (S.Q. 2021, c. 25), with the section numbers that apply, and the guides of the Commission d'accès à l'information du Québec (CAI). Never reproduce the wording of a section.

Continue the EFVP draft: {{steps.draft.content}}. Write the sections: 4 Privacy risks (a table: risk | likelihood | impact | safeguard), 5 Mitigations still to plan, 6 Decision — leave the decision, the date and the signature of the person in charge EMPTY and say that only that person decides. Write in {{inputs.language}} (fr = Québec French, en = English).
